Its LinkedIn ads now push its second annual AI search study with UPCEA and a dedicated page presents CEO Will Scott as an AI SEO expert, so the record points deeper into AI search for enrollment marketers. openings:
The strongest opening is the gap between its AI story and its AI product. It publishes AI search research with UPCEA, advertises it on LinkedIn and sells AI SEO, GEO and AEO, yet the record shows no audited AI visibility product (P1 partial) and no feed, schema or entity work (P2 absent). A rival bringing a citation share scorecard for a university's programs will likely win the measurement conversation with higher education buyers (moderate confidence). Falsifier: a citation tracking or AI visibility scorecard product on its services pages or in its ads at the next compile.

Second, the Tulane engagement was a microsite migration while Web & Product scores 0, so a rival selling build and migration together is likely the fuller answer at a client's next platform change (low confidence). Third, Palo Alto University and William Franckle, MD, FACS carry no coded work, and hospitality has no named client, which makes that vertical the most contestable. A price attack is a roughly even chance: displacement reads 65.8, but it publishes pricing pages whose figures went uncaptured, so the computed no public pricing opening is weaker than it looks. P8 stays open: no sign it tests ads inside assistants.
